title: Force through the finish
effort: Complete knee, hip and ankle extension without losing the force-producing base or compensating through the trunk.
quality_marker: Record E1’s six attempts under the Week 4 setup when possible: one controlled dip, clear extension and a held quiet reception. Do not chase a locked knee, exaggerated toe point or arched finish; changed setup makes output comparisons descriptive only. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
brief: The familiar countermovement jump provides the main upward-force reference. Grounded lead-leg extension, a bench-supported hip finish, rear-ankle output, four fixed-split receptions and a familiar hip reversal give distinct supporting jobs. Walking entries are removed and primary work uses bilateral bases.

explosive.name: Countermovement Jump — vertical rise and stick
explosive.key: Countermovement Jump — vertical rise and stick
explosive.job: Main coordinated knee/hip push after one controlled countermovement.
explosive.cue: Use one comfortable dip with arm swing, jump vertically, receive on both feet and hold 2 s. No repeated bouncing, deep-collapse dip or knee tuck for apparent height.
explosive.replacement: a smaller countermovement jump or fast nonflight squat rise when reception cannot stay controlled; record removed landings
explosive.novelty_reason: Restore the familiar six-attempt countermovement anchor after walking-entry work. Repetition preserves a recognizable upward-force task while the coach checks full controlled extension; a new dip depth would confound the reference.
explosive.rest_text: 90 s between complete set rounds; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Step-Up — fast grounded drive, rear foot joins
explosive.key: Step-Up — fast grounded drive, rear foot joins
explosive.job: Let one lead leg supply upward force against a stable support without hand-off to a jump.
explosive.cue: Use a low inspected immovable step. Front whole foot planted; rise quickly without springing from the trailing foot, bring that foot onto the step, then descend under control in 3 s. No flight.
explosive.replacement: a supported fast split-squat rise with both feet grounded and the same per-leg dose if support fit fails
explosive.identity: bodyweight-step-up parent; nonflight rapid delivery proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Retain four familiar grounded step-ups to express knee/hip finish on each lead leg without another flight task. Adding dumbbells merely to rename the drill would not be useful novelty.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Hip Thrust — bench-supported rapid rise
explosive.job: Express hip extension through the finish with shoulder support allowing a different range from the floor bridge.
explosive.cue: Use bodyweight first. Support the upper back, not the neck, on a low stable bench that cannot slide; feet flat and knees comfortable. Lower 2 s, drive hips up quickly and hold 1 s with ribs and pelvis aligned. No lumbar arch or head throw.
explosive.replacement: three rapid floor-bridge rises with the same reset/rest if bench height, friction or shoulder support is unsuitable
explosive.identity: dumbbell-hip-thrust family; rapid bodyweight bench execution proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Shoulder elevation changes hip travel and support geometry from the floor bridge. No heavy explosive load is added simply to make the drill new.
explosive.rest_text: 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Split-Stance Calf Rise — rapid rear-heel finish
explosive.key: Split-Stance Calf Rise — rapid rear-heel finish
explosive.job: Produce rear-ankle force through the forefoot in a stable forward-oriented stance.
explosive.cue: Use stable hand support and a short split stance. Front foot stays flat; rear knee softly straight and rear forefoot planted. Rapidly lift the rear heel, hold 1 s and lower 2 s while the pelvis stays still. Three reps per rear leg; no stride or flight.
explosive.replacement: an assisted single-leg straight-knee rapid heel rise at the same per-leg dose if the split stance does not load the rear ankle usefully
explosive.identity: standing-dumbbell-calf-raise family; rapid bodyweight rear-ankle split-stance execution proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Places the force-producing ankle behind the pelvis with the front foot supporting posture, unlike a vertical single-leg rise. It rehearses the rear-foot finish without an acceleration run.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 6 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Split Squat Jump — fixed stance, same-stance reception
explosive.key: Split Squat Jump — fixed stance, same-stance reception
explosive.job: Complete a modest upward leg drive while retaining a stable front/back foot relationship.
explosive.cue: From a comfortable fixed split stance make one small dip and jump a modest height. Receive with both feet in the same split stance and hold 2 s; no scissor switch or rear-foot kick. Two attempts per lead leg.
explosive.replacement: two fast grounded supported split-squat rises per lead leg if the split reception cannot be controlled; log removed landings
explosive.identity: split-squat-jump-to-stick family; same-stance no-switch execution declared
explosive.novelty_reason: Changes the receiving base to the original split stance rather than Week 3 parallel reception. Only four controlled landings are used; jumping switches would add irrelevant switching complexity.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 60 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Kettlebell Swing — continuous two-hand chest-height float
explosive.key: Kettlebell Swing — continuous two-hand chest-height float
explosive.job: Reapply hip force after the retained implement returns, with no ground landing.
explosive.cue: Use a light bell and established hinge; three continuous hip-driven swings to chest-level float. Guide the return, keep ribs stacked and park after the third. No arm lift or squat bounce.
explosive.replacement: three separated parked swings with full 10 s resets if continuous timing is unconfirmed; add actual time
explosive.identity: kettlebell-swing; migration 472 continuous two-hand source variant
explosive.novelty_reason: Three familiar continuous hip swings retain a lengthened-hip force contribution alongside the new near-finish hip thrust. A new swing style would add instruction without a more direct job.

resilience.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — light
resilience.job: Light outer-ankle strengthening to resist rolling over the foot edge during the push.
resilience.cue: Heel supported; hand-held light band draws the forefoot inward. Move forefoot outward 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s while the knee stays still.
resilience.replacement: gentle hand resistance through a smaller range at the same per-leg dose
resilience.identity: Proposed exact dynamic execution; ankle-eversion family referenced, no exact ID
resilience.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 30 s, then the other leg; 10 total reps; 45 s before the next exercise/section

resilience.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction — light
resilience.job: Light lateral-hip strengthening to keep the pelvis and knee organized over the force-producing leg.
resilience.cue: Lie on side, lower leg bent; lift upper leg slightly 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s with toes facing forward and pelvis still. Bodyweight is sufficient unless clearly easy.
resilience.replacement: a smaller unloaded leg lift with the same per-leg dose
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical ID
resilience.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 30 s, then the other leg; 10 total reps; 60 s before the next exercise/section

primary.name: Goblet Squat — dumbbell
primary.job: Bilateral knee/hip extension through a repeatable full-foot push.
primary.cue: Lower 3 s, stand decisively in about 1 s; hold a manageable goblet load and retain comfortable depth without heels lifting.
primary.replacement: a lighter goblet squat through controlled comfortable range; a two-dumbbell front hold may replace a limiting goblet grip
primary.identity: Verified local family: goblet-squat; supported/load/range details are declared coaching executions
primary.rest_text: 120 s between complete set rounds; 120 s before the next lift preparation
primary.preparation_text: Load preparation of this same lift: 1 × 5 then 1 × 3; very light first, intermediate only if a second set is listed; at least 5 technical reps/cycles in reserve; 60 s between preparation rounds; 90 s before working sets. Extra load-finding work adds actual workload/time.

primary.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
primary.job: Hip extension from a lengthened hinge, with the trunk transmitting rather than supplying the motion.
primary.cue: Lower 3 s with soft knees, bells close and hips back; stand in about 1 s. Stop range before back rounding or pelvic tuck.
primary.replacement: a lighter two-dumbbell hinge through a shorter controlled range

primary.job: Hip extension near the finish with the knee angle held, without another lengthened-hinge dose.
primary.cue: Secure a manageable load over the pelvis; rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Finish with ribs/pelvis aligned, not lumbar arching.
primary.replacement: a lighter loaded floor bridge with the same controlled range; a shorter lever may be used if hamstrings cramp

primary.job: Plantar-flexion force with the knees extended for the final upward/forward push.
primary.cue: Use stable hand support if needed; rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s to the floor. Keep knees softly straight and heels tracking over the forefoot.
primary.replacement: a lighter supported standing calf raise; use individual load or leverage that retains the required technical reserve

primary.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise — bent knees
primary.job: Plantar-flexion force while the knee remains flexed during early push and receiving.
primary.cue: Sit on an inspected stable bench, feet on floor; secure loads on thighs, rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s without knee-angle change or bouncing.
primary.replacement: a supported standing bent-knee calf raise with the same bilateral dose and 2–3 technical RIR if bench/load support is unsuitable

primary.name: Hamstring Walkout — complete out-and-back cycle
primary.job: Knee-flexor leverage while the pelvis stays raised, distinct from moving through a hip hinge.
primary.cue: Start in a bilateral bridge. Each cycle is two small heel steps out per foot, then two back per foot: eight placements in about 8 s. Keep a soft knee and level hips; never chase a fully straight leg.
primary.replacement: a shorter-lever walkout at the same complete-cycle count; reduce range for sagging or cramp and stop if control does not return

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

setup: The new rapid hip thrust requires a bench that fits the athlete and cannot slide; the floor-bridge replacement is already fully dosed. Keep split-stance takeoff/receiving inside a marked short area. Rear-heel work stays grounded and outside active lanes. No running entry or object release is needed. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
delivery: Estimate 54–61 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.
progression: Week 9 prescribed six primary rounds/seven bouts. Here Goblet Squat returns to two rounds at 2 × 5, RDL remains 1 × 5 and floor bridge 1 × 5 replaces Reverse Lunge. Seven rounds/seven bilateral bouts contain 32 conventional reps plus two walkout cycles. Landings rise six to ten but walking entries and throws are removed; the different event types are not treated as equivalent stress. Use modest split-jump height and hold load; reduce the remaining jump effort or strength round if actual quality warrants it.
audit_findings: Ten bilateral receptions include six parallel and four fixed-split landings, not ten identical jumps or any unilateral receiving. Three new related executions have defined support/base roles; three exact repeats preserve useful practice. The explosive hip thrust is bodyweight/rapid and the primary floor bridge is loaded/controlled with a different support range; neither performance is counted twice. No forceful joint lockout is prescribed.
